tldr: DeepSeek said on Oct 20 it is open-sourcing DeepInfer, the software that serves its production models. Coverage first framed it as a way to cut AI operating costs, then as pressure on OpenAI and Anthropic.
whats_new: Latent Space put numbers on DeepInfer on Oct 21: 155T tokens/day per cluster at roughly 80% margin and an 81-day payback, as reported by the newsletter.
why_it_matters: A production-proven open inference stack gives platform teams a reference for serving cost and throughput that vLLM-style deployments can be benchmarked against.

status.detail: DeepInfer is public; independent reproduction of the efficiency claims has not appeared yet.

beats.headline: DeepSeek open-sources the stack that runs its models
beats.summary: Bloomberg, Quartz, Gizmodo and PYMNTS report the release on Oct 20 as an open-source tool to lower AI operating costs.

beats.headline: SiliconANGLE names it DeepInfer, the framework behind production services
Scale and margin figures arrive
beats.summary: Latent Space and follow-up writeups cite 155T tokens a day and a high-margin serving business.

beats.headline: Adjacent production-AI items clustered into the window
beats.summary: Not DeepSeek coverage: GitHub secret protection (Oct 7), a mixed-hardware inference framework (Oct 18), llm-d 1.0 (Oct 20) and an Anthropic formal-verification result (Oct 22).

open_questions: Does an independent benchmark reproduce the 155T tokens/day and ~80% margin figures?
Which hardware backends does DeepInfer support outside DeepSeek's own clusters?
Which license terms govern commercial reuse of DeepInfer?
take_for_builders: Read the DeepInfer repo and license before changing a serving stack; treat the margin figures as unverified until someone reproduces them on non-DeepSeek hardware.
